papers.title: Example paper A: a layered material studied by optical spectroscopy

paragraphs.text: We use photoluminescence spectroscopy to measure monolayer WS2 grown by chemical vapour deposition. The emission energy of the neutral exciton is 2.03 eV at room temperature.
These observations suggest that defect engineering controls the exciton trapping efficiency in WS2.

papers.title: Example paper B: the same material class under different conditions

paragraphs.text: Tungsten disulfide (WS2) monolayers were studied with photoluminescence spectroscopy under 4 K. The emission energy of the neutral exciton is 2.10 eV in this low temperature regime.
Compared with the untreated sample, the treated sample shows a higher photoluminescence intensity at 4 K.
